issues.description: The `url` attribute is set to the same value as `homepage` ("https://asciidoc.org/"). In Conan convention, `url` typically points to the recipe repository (e.g., the ConanCenter or project repo hosting the recipe), distinct from the upstream package homepage. While no rule explicitly prohibits this, it is unconventional.
issues.suggestion: Consider setting `url` to the recipe repository URL if applicable, or document that this is intentional for this project's conventions.

issues.description: `build_system: python` is not in the standard list (cmake | autotools | makefile | meson). While this is a reasonable value for a pure Python package using setup.py, the code style standard does not list 'python' as a valid build_system value.
issues.suggestion: Consider extending the manifest.yaml build_system standard list to include 'python' for Python package recipes, or document this as an accepted extension.

issues.description: The build section specifies `cc: clang` and `cxx: clang++` for a pure Python package that has no C/C++ compilation. These fields are unnecessary and potentially misleading since the package uses `python3 setup.py install` with no compiler involvement.
issues.suggestion: Consider removing the `cc` and `cxx` fields from the build section, or set them to 'N/A' to accurately reflect that no C/C++ compilation occurs.

issues.description: The test_asciidoc.py file contains only a docstring with no actual test code. While the real test logic is correctly implemented in test_package/conanfile.py's test() method (which executes the asciidoc binary for version check and HTML conversion), the file itself is essentially empty. The test_package as a whole satisfies R34 because conanfile.py's test() method does execute the tested package's binary.
issues.suggestion: Consider adding actual pytest test code to test_asciidoc.py (e.g., subprocess-based tests invoking asciidoc) to make the file self-documenting, or clarify in the CI L0c requirement that a marker docstring file is acceptable when test logic resides in conanfile.py.

issues.description: In the `_create_wrapper` method, the `except OSError: pass` silently ignores errors from `os.chmod()`. While this is a common pattern for cross-filesystem operations where chmod may not be supported, no comment explains why the error is ignored, which is the spirit of code-style-rule-10 (no silently swallowed errors without explanation).
issues.suggestion: Add a brief comment explaining why the OSError is ignored, e.g., `except OSError: pass  # chmod may fail on non-POSIX filesystems`. Note: code-style-rule-10 technically applies to shell scripts, but the principle extends to Python error handling.

R34_stub_test.details: test_package/conanfile.py test() method executes the asciidoc binary with two real tests: (1) `asciidoc --version` smoke test, (2) functional test converting an AsciiDoc document to HTML with output verification via `os.path.exists()` and `raise AssertionError`. This is NOT a stub test.

R9_bypass_tests.details: No `def test(self): pass`, no commented-out test calls, no `os.system('exit 0')` or similar forced pass. The test() method has real assertions and raises exceptions on failure.

fake_status.details: manifest.yaml status is 'built' (verified, not yet uploaded to repo). This is consistent with notes.md showing successful build and verification. No 'failed' marked as 'published'.

R19_manual_packaging.details: No pre-compiled .so/.a/binary files in the PR. All build artifacts are produced from source via setup.py install in conanfile.py build().

R40_deep_adaptation.details: asciidoc is not in any R40 category (graphics/rendering, UI framework, multimedia, peripherals/hardware, system low-level). It is a pure Python text document processor.

R26_static_linking.details: asciidoc is not a system-named library. It is an application (package_type='application').

R32_ohos_compatibility.details: No OS-specific conditionals in conanfile.py. settings='os', 'arch' is appropriate for a pure Python package. No `self.settings.os == 'Linux'` checks that would miss OHOS.

R33_shell_env_vars.details: No bare shell env var dependencies in self.run(). The main conanfile.py uses `self.run(f'python3 setup.py install --prefix={install_dir}')` with a computed path. The test_package conanfile.py uses `PYTHONPATH=...` inline with a value computed from package_folder (deterministic, not dependent on pre-existing env vars that might be empty on release workers).
